course.title: Applied Artificial Intelligence
course.description: Apply AI to real business processes: map opportunities, measure benefits, manage risk and implement responsibly. Builds on conceptual AI knowledge toward practical organisational use.

modules.title: Module 1: AI in business operations
modules.description: Find where AI creates real value.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: Mapping business processes
lessons.description: See work as steps that can be measured and improved.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Map a simple process into steps, inputs, outputs and pain points.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.2: Where AI helps and where it does not
lessons.description: Match AI strengths to process needs.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Identify process steps that are good AI candidates and steps that should stay human.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.3: Measuring benefits
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Write measurable benefit hypotheses (time saved, error reduced, revenue impact) and baseline them.

lessons.title: Module 1 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 1 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Mapping a process helps because:
It wastes time
*It reveals steps, handoffs and pain points where AI might help
It replaces all metrics
It hides problems
explain: Visibility enables improvement.
level: 1

Q: AI is often a good fit for:
Irreversible high-stakes judgements with no data
*Repetitive, pattern-rich tasks with feedback data
Tasks with zero historical examples
Replacing all strategy
explain: Patterns + data favour AI.
level: 1

Q: Before implementing AI you should:
Skip measurement
*Define success metrics and capture a baseline
Only buy the most expensive tool
Ignore users
explain: Baseline + metrics prove value.
level: 1

Q: A pain point in a process is:
Always best left unchanged
*A step that is slow, error-prone, costly or frustrating
Only the last step
A type of database
explain: Pain points are improvement targets.
level: 1

Q: Human judgement remains essential when:
Tasks are purely repetitive
*Stakes are high, context is novel, or accountability cannot be automated
Data is perfect and abundant
The model is large
explain: Humans own high-stakes and novel cases.
level: 2

Q: Time saved is a useful benefit metric when:
It is never measured
*It is measured against a real baseline and translates into capacity or cost impact
It ignores quality
It is only estimated once after launch
explain: Credible measurement matters.
level: 2

Q: Not every process step should be automated because:
AI is free
*Some steps need empathy, accountability or rare expertise
Humans never make errors
Automation is illegal
explain: Fit-for-purpose design.
level: 1

Q: A benefit hypothesis should be:
Vague and unmeasurable
*Specific, measurable and tied to a process outcome
Hidden from stakeholders
Only about model accuracy
explain: Specificity enables evaluation.
level: 1

Q: Process mapping usually includes:
Only the CEO’s opinion
*Steps, actors, inputs, outputs and pain points
Only the software vendor’s slides
No documentation
explain: Structured mapping is practical.
level: 2

Q: The main goal of applied AI in operations is:
Using AI for its own sake
*Improving outcomes that matter to the organisation and its customers
Maximising model size
Avoiding all measurement
explain: Outcomes over technology.
level: 1

modules.title: Module 2: Designing AI-enabled workflows
modules.description: Human + AI handoffs that work in practice.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.1: Human-in-the-loop design
lessons.description: Keep people where they add most value.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Design workflows where AI drafts or ranks and humans approve, correct or handle exceptions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.2: Data readiness for applied AI
lessons.description: What data quality and access are required.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Assess whether available data is sufficient, accessible and sufficiently clean for the intended use.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.3: Pilot design and evaluation
lessons.description: Start small, learn fast, decide deliberately.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Design a limited pilot with clear success criteria and a go/no-go decision point.

lessons.title: Module 2 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 2 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Human-in-the-loop means:
Removing all humans
*Keeping humans in critical review, exception handling or approval steps
Only using paper
Ignoring AI outputs
explain: Humans remain accountable for key steps.
level: 1

Q: Data readiness includes:
Only having a logo
*Access, quality, volume, representativeness and update frequency
Only model size
Ignoring privacy
explain: Multiple dimensions matter.
level: 1

Q: A good pilot is:
A full nationwide rollout on day one
*Limited in scope, measured carefully, and used to decide next steps
Never evaluated
Hidden from users
explain: Pilots reduce risk.
level: 1

Q: Exception handling is important because:
AI never fails
*Real data includes unusual cases the model may mishandle
Users prefer pure automation always
It slows learning
explain: Exceptions are inevitable.
level: 2

Q: Go/no-go criteria should be defined:
After the pilot ends randomly
*Before the pilot starts
Only by the vendor
Never
explain: Pre-defined criteria prevent bias.
level: 1

Q: Poor data quality in a pilot often leads to:
Perfect results
*Misleading performance estimates
Faster training only
No effect
explain: Quality limits insight.
level: 2

Q: Involving end users in pilot design helps:
Slow everything uselessly
*Surface practical constraints and improve adoption
Guarantee perfect accuracy
Replace metrics
explain: Users know the real work.
level: 1

Q: Ranking or drafting by AI with human approval is a common pattern because:
It removes all work
*It speeds routine work while preserving human judgement on the final output
It is illegal
It requires no data
explain: Speed + oversight.
level: 2

Q: Access to data must also respect:
Only convenience
*Privacy, security and policy constraints
Only speed
No rules
explain: Compliance is non-negotiable.
level: 1

Q: The purpose of a pilot is primarily to:
Impress investors with slides
*Learn whether the approach works well enough to scale
Use as much budget as possible
Avoid measurement
explain: Learning drives the decision.
level: 1

modules.title: Module 3: Risk, governance and change
modules.description: Manage downside and help people adopt new ways of working.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.1: Risks of applied AI
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

List major risk categories and one mitigation for each in a concrete scenario.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.2: Lightweight governance
lessons.description: Roles, logging and review without heavy bureaucracy.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Define simple ownership, logging and review practices appropriate to the risk level.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.3: Supporting people through change
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Plan communication and training so staff understand what changes and why.

lessons.title: Module 3 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 3 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Over-reliance on AI outputs can cause:
No problems
*Missed errors and reduced human skill over time
Only faster work with zero downside
Perfect compliance
explain: Critical thinking must remain.
level: 1

Q: Bias risk is best addressed by:
Ignoring it
*Checking performance across relevant groups and improving data/process
Using only one data source forever
Hiding metrics
explain: Measurement and improvement.
level: 2

Q: Lightweight governance should match:
The heaviest possible bureaucracy always
*The risk level of the use case
Only the vendor’s preference
No documentation
explain: Proportionality matters.
level: 1

Q: Logging AI-assisted decisions helps:
Only increase storage costs
*Audit, learning and accountability
Hide all errors
Replace humans
explain: Logs support review.
level: 2

Q: Change support should include:
Only a single email
*Clear explanation of what changes, training, and channels for feedback
No training
Punishment for questions
explain: People need support to adopt.
level: 1

Q: Privacy risk rises when:
No personal data is used
*Personal or sensitive data is processed without adequate controls
Only public aggregate data is used
Models are small
explain: Sensitive data needs controls.
level: 1

Q: Assigning clear ownership for an AI workflow means:
Nobody is responsible
*Someone is accountable for performance, incidents and improvement
Only the model is accountable
Ownership rotates daily randomly
explain: Accountability is essential.
level: 1

Q: A mitigation for model error is:
Never checking outputs
*Human review for high-impact cases and monitoring error rates
Deleting all logs
Assuming perfection
explain: Review + monitoring.
level: 2

Q: Staff resistance often decreases when:
Changes are forced with no explanation
*People understand the purpose, receive training, and can give feedback
All jobs are threatened without alternatives
Metrics are hidden
explain: Purpose + support + voice.
level: 2

Q: Governance is not only paperwork; it is:
Optional decoration
*The set of practices that keep AI use safe, effective and aligned with goals
Only for large banks
A replacement for ethics
explain: Practices enable responsible use.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 4.1: Implementation checklist
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Use a practical checklist covering data, tooling, process redesign, training and support.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.2: Monitoring and feedback
lessons.description: Detect drift and user issues early.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Define a small set of health metrics and a feedback channel for users.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.3: Scaling what works
lessons.description: Expand carefully after evidence of value.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Plan staged expansion only after the pilot meets its criteria.

lessons.title: Module 4 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 4 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Implementation readiness includes:
Only buying software
*Data, process, people and technical readiness
Only marketing
Ignoring users
explain: Multiple dimensions.
level: 1

Q: Monitoring after launch is needed because:
Nothing ever changes
*Data, behaviour and performance drift over time
Models improve automatically forever
Users never find issues
explain: Drift is real.
level: 1

Q: Scaling should happen:
Immediately for all cases
*After evidence that the pilot meets success criteria
In secret
Without metrics
explain: Evidence before scale.
level: 1

Q: A user feedback channel helps:
Only increase complaints
*Surface problems and improvement ideas quickly
Replace all metrics
Hide failures
explain: Feedback improves the system.
level: 2

Q: A simple health metric set might include:
Only the CEO’s mood
*Error rate, volume processed, user satisfaction, and critical incident count
Only model size
Nothing quantitative
explain: A balanced few metrics.
level: 2

Q: Process redesign is often required because:
AI drops into any process unchanged
*Work steps, roles and handoffs usually need adjustment
People never change how they work
Only IT needs to change
explain: Process and AI must fit.
level: 1

Q: Training should cover:
Only the technical API
*How the new workflow works, when to trust or escalate, and how to report issues
Nothing practical
Only history of AI
explain: Practical competence.
level: 1

Q: Expanding to a new department without adaptation risks:
Guaranteed success
*Poor fit and rejection
Zero effort
Automatic improvement
explain: Context differs.
level: 2

Q: Continuous improvement means:
Freezing the system forever after launch
*Regularly reviewing metrics and feedback and making targeted updates
Changing everything weekly randomly
Ignoring all data
explain: Steady refinement.
level: 1

Q: The ultimate measure of applied AI success is:
Model parameter count
*Sustained improvement in the outcomes the organisation cares about
Number of tools purchased
Slide deck length
explain: Outcomes win.
level: 1
